text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.76% today to $134.69, giving back some of the sharp gains it posted over the past week as oil prices pulled back slightly. U.S. crude dropped to $91.48 a barrel today after climbing more than 9% this week on escalating Iran-U.S. military tensions; the stock had climbed from $130 just a week ago on those geopolitical risks, and today's modest retreat reflects some cooling of that immediate conflict premium.

The broader energy backdrop remains supportive for refiners and oil producers, though. Diesel prices hit record highs as Ukraine continues destroying Russian refineries and Russia banned diesel exports, while the EU formally joined U.S. sanctions on Iran—both of which reduce global refining capacity and keep crude prices elevated despite today's dip. These supply-side pressures from geopolitical conflict are structural headwinds that could continue supporting energy prices even as daily volatility settles.
